hypothesis: V2 Tanager reproduces OLCI's variability at the scale OLCI can see
statistic: per band: correlation, and regression slope (Tanager's spread as a factor of OLCI's, both in sr-1) — worst gated band, worst scene
note: sf_bay 443 r=0.67 x0.95, 490 r=0.82 x1.53, 560 r=0.88 x1.80; lake_ontario 443 r=0.78 x0.90, 490 r=0.92 x1.13, 560 r=0.95 x1.09; loreto 443 r=0.58 x1.03, 490 r=0.81 x1.49, 560 r=0.82 x1.44. Gated on 490/560 nm, the bands the 560/490 ratio is built from; 443 nm is reported but not gated. Planet ships surface reflectance, which tanager_io.to_rrs divides by pi, so both sides are Rrs in sr-1 and parity is a slope of 1. The spread statistic was added on revision: correlation is scale-invariant and cannot license a claim about variance.

hypothesis: V3 within-pixel variability is spatially structured, not noise
statistic: median adjacent difference / same after shuffling, per scene and sensor
note: 4 of 5 assessable combinations are structured; above the bar: loreto/pace 0.79; not assessable on sf_bay/pace. A shuffled field scores 1.0 by construction.

hypothesis: V4 within-pixel variability exceeds the declared noise floor
statistic: median within-pixel CV / declared relative uncertainty at 560 nm
note: floor is the product's own surface_reflectance_uncertainty

hypothesis: V5 the homogeneity filter accepts boxes with variable interiors
statistic: boxes passing CV<0.15; within-pixel CV over between-pixel CV of the same green/blue ratio; fraction of passing boxes containing a pixel whose own interior CV exceeds 0.15
note: the ratio is like for like — same scalar, same window, same instrument, only the scale differs; the protocol's own filter statistic is on the coarse sensor's retrieval and is reported separately in h_results.json. Within-pixel CV is a lower bound: the additive atmospheric pedestal inflates the mean and so deflates every CV. The same decomposition on plain 560 nm reflectance instead of the color ratio gives lake_ontario/olci 0.6x; lake_ontario/pace 0.4x; loreto/olci 1.9x; loreto/pace 1.2x; sf_bay/olci 0.8x — the answer depends on which quantity is asked about, and both are reported
